advices.diagnosis: The class has a critical LCOM4 of 4, meaning its methods are not sharing attributes and the class is poorly cohesive. It also has a modest NOM (5) and WMC (5) due solely to trivial getter methods, and a perfect DAM (1.0) because all attributes are private. No internal class references (DCC=0) are present.

suggestions.title: Replace explicit getters with dataclass fields or @property accessors
suggestions.sketch: Convert the class to a frozen @dataclass with public attributes (customer_id, name, email, tier). If you need read‑only semantics, keep the attributes public and rely on the dataclass's immutability, or replace each getter with a simple @property that returns the underlying attribute. This removes the five trivial getter methods, collapsing the method‑attribute graph into a single component.

advices.risk_notes: Call sites that currently invoke customer.customer_id() (or name(), email(), tier()) will break and must be updated to use the attribute access (customer.customer_id) or the new property name. If the class is part of a public API, this change is a breaking change and may require version bumping or deprecation shim.
